entries.title: Engine — description
entries.content: Conventional 4-cylinder, L-head, internal-combustion engine. The engine, clutch, transmission, and transfer case are built into a unit power plant mounted at four points in the chassis.

entries.title: Engine tabulated data
entries.content: Type: L-head, 4 cylinders. Bore: 3⅛ in. Stroke: 4⅜ in. Piston displacement: 134.2 cu in. Net horsepower: 54 at 4,000 rpm. SAE horsepower: 15.63. Firing order: 1-3-4-2. Compression ratio: 6.48 to 1. Compression: 110 lb per sq in at 185 rpm.

entries.title: Valve tappet clearance
entries.content: Tappet clearance, intake and exhaust: 0.014 in (hot or cold).

entries.title: Cylinder compression test
entries.content:
1. Test cylinder compression with a gage.
2. The gage must read more than 70 pounds, and the variation between cylinders must remain less than 10 pounds.
3. Normal compression is approximately 110 pounds per square inch at cranking speed.
4. Report lack of compression to higher authority.

entries.title: Engine tune-up
entries.content:
1. Perform preventive maintenance operations (par. 16).
2. Remove spark plugs and clean; adjust gaps (par. 67).
3. Test cylinder compression (must exceed 70 lb; variation between cylinders under 10 lb; normal ~110 psi).
4. Check that the ground strap at the engine left front support is in good condition and tight.
5. Remove distributor cap and rotor; check for cracks and leaks; clean or replace breaker points and adjust (par. 64).
6. Check ignition timing (par. 65).
7. Check valve tappet clearance (par. 56).
8. Install spark plugs, assemble distributor, start engine, warm to normal temperature, then set the throttle valve stop screw for 600 rpm idle (8 mph vehicle speed).
9. Adjust the idle adjustment screw until the engine idles smoothly. If float level, accelerating pump, or metering rod need adjustment, report to higher authority.
10. Tighten cylinder head screws and nuts with a torque wrench (par. 54).
11. Check operation of the manifold heat control (par. 53).

entries.title: Valve tappet adjustment
entries.content:
1. Remove the valve spring cover (par. 55).
2. Adjust the self-locking tappet screws while cold (or warm) to 0.014 inch.
3. Start with No. 1 cylinder on its compression stroke at top center, then adjust valves in the cylinder firing order (1-3-4-2), turning the crankshaft one-half turn for each cylinder.
NOTE: the valve tappets will then be on the heel of the cam.
4. Replace the valve spring cover (par. 55).

entries.title: Intake and exhaust manifolds — removal and installation
entries.content:
The intake and exhaust manifolds are attached to each other with four screws, forming a unit containing the heat control valve.

Removal:
1. Remove the carburetor air horn; disconnect hand throttle, choke, and accelerator at the carburetor.
2. Loosen the fuel line at the fuel pump and disconnect at the carburetor.
3. Remove the two nuts attaching the carburetor to the intake manifold; remove the carburetor with its accelerator spring clip.
4. Loosen the valve spring cover front screw to relieve pull on the crankcase ventilator tube, then remove the tube.
5. Disconnect the exhaust pipe at the manifold.
6. Remove all nuts and washers from the manifold studs, remove the manifolds as an assembly, and remove the ventilator valve.

Installation:
1. Clean contact surfaces of manifolds and cylinder block.
2. Place a new gasket on the studs and install the manifold assembly.
3. Install washers (convex side against the manifolds) and nuts; tighten evenly to 31–35 ft-lb.
4. Tighten the four intake-to-exhaust manifold screws.
5. Attach the exhaust pipe with a new gasket.
6. Install the ventilator tube; tighten the valve spring cover front screw.
7. Reinstall the carburetor and connections; prime the carburetor with the fuel pump hand lever, start the engine, and check for leaky gaskets.

entries.title: Manifold stud nut torque
entries.content: Manifold stud nuts: tighten evenly to 31–35 ft-lb, with the convex side of the washers against the manifolds.

entries.title: Manifold heat control valve
entries.content: The heat control valve is controlled thermostatically by a bimetal spring. It diverts exhaust gases around the central portion of the intake manifold during engine warm-up. NOTE: the valve is an integral part of the exhaust manifold — for replacement, remove the manifold assembly (par. 52).

entries.title: Cylinder head gasket — removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Drain the cooling system at the radiator drain cock (left front). Save antifreeze for reuse.
2. Disconnect spark plug wires; remove the distributor cap.
3. Remove the two cylinder-stud nuts holding the air cleaner tube bracket; remove bracket with wires and cap.
4. Remove the radiator upper tube with hoses attached.
5. Disconnect the oil filter upper tube, remove the two filter nuts, and remove the filter.
6. Remove all cylinder head screws and nuts; remove the head and bonding strap. CAUTION: do not damage the oil filler tube. Discard the gasket.

Installation:
1. Clean the cylinder head, piston tops, and block thoroughly.
2. Place the gasket on the block — the front and rear centre studs are pilot studs that position it.
3. Install the head (CAUTION: do not damage the oil filler pipe), rear bonding strap, oil filter, and air cleaner bracket.
4. Tighten screws and nuts evenly and in sequence (fig. 25) with a torque wrench: screws 65–70 ft-lb, nuts 60–65 ft-lb.
5. Reconnect the oil filter tube, distributor cap, and spark plug wires to the correct plugs.
6. Install the radiator upper tube, close the drain cock, fill the cooling system, start the engine, and check for leaks. Top up coolant if needed.

entries.title: Cylinder head torque
entries.content: Cylinder head screws: 65–70 ft-lb. Cylinder head nuts: 60–65 ft-lb. Tighten evenly and in the sequence shown in the tightening chart (fig. 25).

entries.title: Valve cover gasket — removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Remove the front valve spring cover bolt.
2. Remove the crankcase ventilator tube at the ventilator valve; remove tube and cap.
3. Remove the rear cover bolt and slide the cover forward, up, and out over the fuel pump. Discard the gasket.

Installation:
1. Clean the cover and its seat on the block.
2. Cement the cork gasket to the cover.
3. Position the cover by sliding it rearward over the fuel pump.
4. Install rear screw and copper gasket (do not tighten), then front screw and copper gasket with ventilator cap, baffle, and gasket.
5. Connect the ventilator tube and tighten both screws evenly.
6. Start the engine and check for oil leaks.

entries.title: Oil pan gasket — removal and installation
entries.content:
Removal:
1. Drain oil via the drain plug in the lower left side of the pan.
2. Remove the oil pan screws — take care not to lose the spacers under the fan belt guard.
3. Remove the pan, then the gasket.

Installation:
1. Clean the pan thoroughly. If the floating oil intake screen is dirty, clean it in dry-cleaning solution.
2. Clean the gasket faces on pan and crankcase; cement the gasket to the pan.
3. Position the pan and install the screws, ensuring the belt-guard spacers are in place.
4. Tighten all screws evenly to 10–14 ft-lb.

entries.title: Oil filter — element change and filter removal
entries.content:
The oil filter is the military standard type on the right front side of the engine. Change the replaceable element every 6,000 miles — more often if oil dirties quickly.

Element change:
1. Unscrew the cover bolt and remove the cover without damaging the gasket.
2. Remove the drain plug to drain the filter; lift out the element.
3. Clean the filter, install the drain plug, and fit the new element.
4. Inspect the cover gasket (replace if needed), install the cover, and tighten the cover bolt.
5. Start the engine, check for leaks, and top up crankcase oil to the FULL mark.

Filter removal/installation:
1. Drain, disconnect upper and lower tubes, remove four bracket bolts, and remove the filter. Remove tube fittings carefully.
2. To install: fit tube fittings, mount in bracket, connect tubes without crossing threads, start engine, check for leaks, and check oil level.

entries.title: Oil filter element service interval
entries.content: Change the oil filter element every 6,000 miles — more often if the oil gets dirty quickly.

entries.title: Crankcase ventilator valve — service
entries.content:
The spring-loaded ventilator valve sits at the centre of the intake manifold, operated by manifold vacuum: closed at idle (high vacuum), opening as engine speed rises to draw clean air from the air cleaner tube through the oil filler pipe to ventilate the crankcase. A valve that fails to seat behaves like a leaky intake manifold.

Service:
1. Loosen the valve spring cover front screw; remove the ventilator tube at the valve; remove the valve.
2. Hold the valve in a vise and remove the top; clean valve and seat; check the spring operates freely; reassemble.
3. Install the valve in the manifold, attach the tube, and tighten the cover front screw.

entries.title: Engine removal
entries.content:
1. Open the hood, lay it back against the windshield, and tie it to avoid accidental closing.
2. Drain the cooling system: drain cocks at radiator lower left and cylinder block right-front lower corner.
3. Remove the battery (cables, wing nuts, hold-down frame).
4. Remove the radiator: hoses, stay rod, two stud nuts — don't lose the radiator pads.
5. Remove the air cleaner. CAUTION: do not tip and spill oil from the reservoir.
6. Remove the cranking motor (wires, two bolts in rear plate, one screw in crankcase side).
7. Right side: disconnect generator wires, ignition switch wire at coil, fuel line at the flexible connection (loosen the tank cap first to relieve pressure), heat indicator unit, engine front support insulator bolts, and bond strap.
8. Left side: remove horn bracket, rear centre head stud nut and bond strap; disconnect throttle/choke controls, pump-to-carburetor fuel line, oil gage line, accelerator rod; separate exhaust pipe from manifold; remove front support bolts and ground strap.
9. Remove the bell housing upper bolts. Sling the engine with rope or cable, take the weight on a chain hoist, remove the remaining bell housing bolts underneath, disconnect the stay cable, drive out the two side bolts, then raise the engine and guide it out of the frame.

entries.title: Engine installation
entries.content:
1. Sling the engine, raise with a chain hoist, and lower into position; insert the transmission shaft into the clutch driven plate hub and work the engine back into place.
2. Install dowel bolts from the engine side, then bell housing bolts; tighten.
3. Install the front support insulator bolts; attach ground strap (left) and bond strap (right).
4. Install the engine stay cable: run the rear adjusting nut up to the bracket, and with the cable just taut, tighten the lock nut on the front side.
5. Right side: cranking motor, coil wire, heat indicator, generator wires, flexible fuel line, air cleaner (check its oil), battery (clean and grease cable connections).
6. Left side: accelerator rod with cotter pin, oil gage tube, exhaust pipe (gasket in good condition), bond strap on head rear stud tightened to 60–65 ft-lb, carburetor choke/throttle wires (panel controls fully in, throttle closed, choke fully open), pump-to-carburetor fuel line, horn.
7. Install the radiator on its pads, hoses, and stay rod; fill with coolant/antifreeze.
8. Tighten the fuel tank cap, check engine oil, start the engine, check for leaks, tune up, and re-check coolant level. Close the hood.
